- Policy stance: The FOMC held the target range at 5.25–5.50% and maintained QT caps ($60B UST, $35B MBS), with IORB at 5.4%, ON RRP at 5.3%, and ON repo minimum at 5.5%. Guidance remains data dependent and mindful of cumulative tightening and policy lags.
- Credit conditions (SLOOS): Banks continue to tighten standards across C&I and CRE, with wider spreads and stricter covenants; household credit (cards, autos, mortgages, HELOCs) also tighter. This corroborates the FOMC’s view that tighter financial and credit conditions will weigh on activity and inflation.
- Beige Book cross-check (New York District): Reports easing employment demand and softer labor market conditions; consumer spending described as subdued; inflationary pressures moderating; housing markets remain weak; inventories are cautious. These regional insights reinforce slowing momentum and disinflation progress.
- Implications: Together, SLOOS and the Beige Book point to increasing downside risks to growth with continued disinflation, supporting a prolonged hold at restrictive levels rather than additional firming unless data re-accelerate. Risk balance skews more negative for near-term activity than a macro-only read would suggest, while price pressures continue to ease.
